correctness.rationale: The frozen result fixes all 24 edges of the four-regular 12-vertex Chvatal graph and defines Ind_r by max connected-component size, not ordinary independence except r=1. Independent reconstruction enumerated all 4096 subsets and all 12 filtration levels, exact face counts 127,425,729,1176,1804,2590,3314,3797,4017,4083,4095,4096, and complete acyclic Hasse matchings for each. Critical-cell data at r2–5 give unimodular Morse minors in d3 at r2 (3x4), d3 and d4 at r3 (3x5,5x1) with chain relation d3*d4=0, d4 at r4 (72x8), d5 at r5 (257x5). Integer CW cancellation using pi_d bouquet=Z^m proves r2=S3, r3=S3, r4=64 S3, r5=252 S4; r6 through r11 only critical cells in one dimension give listed wedges and r12 is the full simplex. For r8–11 independent four-vertex-connectivity check recovers ordinary simplex skeleton homotopy. Separately reducing all ordinary simplicial F2 boundary columns ordered by (birth cutoff, dimension, bitmask) recovers complete barcode including one H3 class [2,5) and 63 H3 classes [4,5); H0 has sole infinite bar. No assertion of integral persistence.

value.rationale: The Chvatal graph is a canonical small 12-vertex triangle-free four-chromatic four-regular graph; its entire higher-independence filtration and exact inclusion behavior are natural combinatorial-topological data beyond its known ordinary independent S2 stage. The integral stages r2–7 display nontrivial changes with large sphere ranks, while the persistent [2,5) H3 interval is a motivated precise map-level fact not determined by stagewise wedge types. Known r1 and near-full simplex-skeleton endpoints are explicitly acknowledged, not presented as novel; they make the finite classification complete.
